# Burden of disease

Cardiovascular disease accounted for approximately **14.1 per cent of
disability-adjusted life years in India in 2016**, and India's cardiovascular
burden is characterised by earlier onset than in most Western populations.

Combined with the treatment-cascade evidence in [[S-01]] and the screening
expansion in [[S-02]], this describes a market whose long-run direction is set
by demographics and diagnosis rather than by promotional intensity.

## Why this matters for prioritisation

This is background rather than a differentiator: it applies uniformly across all
three segments in the dataset and therefore does not change relative ranking.
It is retained in the corpus because it is the evidence base for the assumption
underlying the entire forecast - that the Cardiac therapy area continues to
grow ahead of overall pharmaceutical market growth over the horizon - and that
assumption should be sourced rather than asserted.

Magnitude is deliberately low, and because it applies equally to every segment
its net effect on relative prioritisation is close to zero by construction.
